newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says seeks early extra budget passage.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says seeks early extra budget passage.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told the opening of parliament on Monday his government would seek early passage of an extra budget for the year to March 31 and of the budget for fiscal 1997/98, in order to support the economy.

Reiterating earlier remarks about his government's economic policy, Hashimoto said: "We will take proper economic measures such as early enactment and smooth implementation of the supplementary budget and the fiscal 1997 budget."
The parliamentary session is due to last until June 18.

Tokyo stock prices have plunged substantially since late last year and Japanese government officials have repeatedly said that the 2.67 trillion yen extra budget for 1996/97 and the 77.39 trillion yen budget for 1997/98 are the keys for sustained economic recovery.
Hashimoto also said that reforms were urgently needed in six areas in Japan -- in administration, social welfare and education, and in the fiscal, economic, and financial systems.
"It is obvious that the existing systems are preventing Japan from developing vigorously," he said.
He said the government would go ahead with its plan to raise the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1 and to discontinue a special income tax cut from next fiscal year.
He said the government planned to take measures to prevent tax reforms from adversely affecting those aged over 65 with low incomes.
